entries: **Twelve hidden Plush Pals: Bobo, Zippy, Twinkle, Tantan, Minto, Shandou, Nibo, Boqi, Zapi, Lei Tuan, WuQiu and Ban Ban.** They stay out of the normal line-up. When the panel loads there is a 1 in 10 chance one of them starts at the front, and each time the line rotates there is a 1 in 10 chance one of them hops in instead of the next regular pal. Each has ten poses: the usual five, plus waving to a neighbour, a big stretch, running when quota burns fast, a startled jump and a signature move it strikes now and then while waiting.

**Hidden Plush Pals unlock one a week, with a collector's book.** From Tuesday 1 December one hidden pal unlocks each week, in a fixed order; a pal that has not unlocked yet never appears. The first time you open the panel after a pal unlocks, it hops into the line, so a new pal is never left to chance; pals you have already met keep their rare random turns. The first time you meet one, a collectible card flips up and files itself into the book at the left end of the line. The book shows every hidden pal as a numbered card: found ones in colour, standing out of their frames and bobbing gently (hover to tilt), unlocked but not yet met as silhouettes, and the rest with their unlock date. Finding them all turns the book gold. The book scrolls when it is taller than the panel. With Reduce Motion on, the card and the tilt are skipped.

**Share a hidden pal's card (macOS).** When the card flips up it now grows to fill the panel and waits, with Share and Keep underneath. Share offers Post to Threads, Post to X, Copy Image, Save Image and More…. The picture is the card itself, with the usage link on its last line, on a 4:5 sheet. Threads and X open their post page with a line of text and the link filled in, and the picture is already on the clipboard, so ⌘V adds it. Save Image puts it in Downloads; More… opens the macOS share menu (Messages, AirDrop and other apps). Found pals in the book carry a share badge: click one to open its card again with Share and Close. Windows keeps the old card without sharing.

**Share today's usage as a card (macOS, every panel except World Cup).** A round share button sits at the right end of the footer's Today line, in the panel's own colours. It opens a Plush Pals card on every panel: today's date, a pal, today's token total, and a bar splitting today's tokens between services, with each service's tokens and share underneath. Services you did not use today are left out, and so are project names and costs. On the Plush Pals panel the pal comes from the line; elsewhere it is a random regular pal, never a hidden one. Share, the menu and the 4:5 picture work as they do for the hidden pals.
**Plush Pals opens on Windows and keeps your collection across launches on macOS and Windows.** The panel also remembers daily greetings and which weekly quota resets it has welcomed.

**The collector's book catches up on missed unlocks.** Each newly unlocked pal gets a turn, cards open one at a time, and the book's tooltip and card animations work at the panel's current language and scale.
**Today's share card includes Antigravity.** Sharing is available once today's totals are ready, and the card's date matches the day counted.
**Sharing confirms when an image is saved.** The card stays open and shows an error if the save fails. Confirmations for Threads and X stay centered and readable.

**Claude quota picks the newer eligible reading for the signed-in organization.** A newer Desktop reading can beat Claude Code's cached reading even when the two observations are less than a minute apart. usage can also read the matching Desktop HTTP cache without a history file when Claude Code identifies the organization.

**Claude quota from the desktop app works again on macOS.** Claude Desktop now keeps its HTTP cache in Chromium's simple-cache format, one file per response, and has stopped adding samples to `plan-usage-history.json`. usage only read the older block-file cache, so if you used Claude only in the desktop app the Claude card stayed at `--` or kept an old number. usage now also reads the simple-cache format. It takes the newest usage response Desktop stored in the last two hours, including ones with a query string such as `?via=plan`, and checks each one's checksums before using it. As before, it reads only local files, read-only, and sends nothing over the network.

**Quota used in the desktop app now shows up even after a terminal session.** Before, once a terminal Claude Code session had reported quota, usage kept showing that number and never looked at the desktop app, so usage in the app afterwards went missing (for example 37% in the menu bar while the app's own Usage page said 55%). Now, when the terminal reading is more than two minutes old and Claude Desktop has a newer one for the same organization you are signed in to in Claude Code, usage shows the Desktop number, in the app and in `usage status`. If the organization can't be matched, the terminal number stays.

**The Claude card explains what to do when it can't read quota from an installed Claude Desktop app.** It asks you to open Settings → Usage and wait a minute. If quota still doesn't show, it explains that a Desktop update may have changed how the app stores data and asks you to report it on GitHub.

**Antigravity's Gemini 4 Argon now reads the shared Gemini quota.** Antigravity CLI 1.5.16 dropped Argon's separate pool, so Argon shares the Gemini weekly and 5-hour limits. usage still looked for the old Argon pool, and Orchestrator models read the Claude / GPT pool. Now both read the Gemini pool in the status line, and the report counts Argon and Orchestrator conversations toward Gemini instead of dropping them. When the menu bar switches from Argon to Gemini, the burn rate starts over instead of showing a sudden jump.

**Report an Issue opens a prefilled bug report.** The panel menu (macOS) and tray menu (Windows) gain the item. It opens a new GitHub issue with the bug template's sections and an Environment block: usage version, install method, OS, CPU, Python, language, panel theme and which AI cards are shown. It includes no paths, usernames, quota figures or logs.

**Two new Plush Pals: Prickle the hedgehog and Shelly the otter.** There are now thirteen pals. The row under the cards never squeezes them closer than before: pals that do not fit wait offstage, and every few minutes the last pal in line hops out and the one that has waited longest hops in. Who starts onstage is shuffled each time the panel loads.

**Four more Plush Pals: Swirl the snail, Pinch the crab, Puff the pufferfish and Tuft the cockatoo.** There are now seventeen pals, each with the same five poses, and they take turns in the line like the others.

**Less memory for history, and no reparsing on large Codex histories.** Equal values loaded from the disk caches now share one copy (about 174 MiB → 162 MiB after three refreshes on real data). The per-file cache limit rose from 4,096 to 16,384, so a Codex history with more files than the old limit no longer reparses part of itself on every refresh.

**Claude quota now updates while you work in an IDE extension or Cowork.** Before, usage read Claude quota only from the status line, which IDE extensions and Cowork never draw, so the menu bar kept the last terminal session's number for hours with no warning. Now, when the status line has reported no new quota for 15 minutes and Claude Code's own cache is newer for the same account, usage shows the cache and says how old it is (it can lag by 20–30 minutes). Quota recorded for another account is no longer shown after you switch accounts, and quota notifications are tracked per account, so switching from an exhausted account no longer reads as a reset.

title.zh-TW: 回報問題會自動填好環境資訊
title.en: Reporting an issue now prefills your environment info

body.zh-TW:
用 usage 碰到錯誤想找開發者反映，卻懶得自己查電腦規格嗎？macOS 的面板選單與 Windows 的系統匣選單現在都加入了「回報問題」（英文介面為 Report an Issue）。

點下去會在程式碼平台 GitHub 開啟一份新問題單，裡頭已套好錯誤回報範本的各個段落並填妥環境區塊。區塊包含 usage 版本、安裝方式、作業系統、CPU、Python、語言、面板主題，以及顯示哪些 AI 卡片，且不含任何檔案路徑、使用者名稱、額度數字或紀錄檔。⟦如同把家電送回原廠維修，以前得自己抄下機型與序號填表，現在櫃檯先幫你印好規格欄，你只需寫上哪裡故障。⟧
body.en:
Run into a bug in usage and want to report it to the developers without looking up your computer specs yourself? Both the macOS panel menu and the Windows tray menu now include "Report an Issue".

Clicking it opens a new issue on GitHub with the bug report template's sections and a prefilled Environment block. The block includes your usage version, install method, OS, CPU, Python, language, panel theme, and which AI cards are shown, and it contains no file paths, usernames, quota numbers, or logs. ⟦Think of bringing an appliance back to the manufacturer for repair: before, you had to copy down the model and serial number onto the form yourself, whereas now the counter prints the specs section for you and you only need to write what broke.⟧

title.zh-TW: 絨毛小夥伴多了六隻並輪流登場

title.zh-TW: 歷史紀錄更省記憶體並放大檔案快取上限
title.en: History uses less memory with a larger file cache limit

body.zh-TW:
長期累積大量 Codex 對話檔後，usage 現在會把相同資料合併共用，重新整理也免去反覆重算的功夫。從磁碟快取（把讀過的資料暫存起來直接用）載入相同數值時，現在只保留一份共用。拿真實資料重新整理三次後，記憶體用量約從 174 MiB 降到 162 MiB。

每個檔案快取的上限也從 4,096 提高到 16,384。Codex 紀錄檔數量超過舊上限時，不會每次重新整理都重新解析其中一部分。⟦跟把辦公室裡一模一樣的表單改成只留一份共用、再把檔案櫃換成四倍大一樣，空間既省下來，舊資料也不必一直被擠出去重抄。⟧
body.en:
When large amounts of Codex conversation files build up over time, usage now merges and shares identical data, saving refreshes from repeating the work. When loading equal values from disk caches, it now keeps only one shared copy. After refreshing three times on real data, memory usage dropped from about 174 MiB to 162 MiB.

The per-file cache limit also rose from 4,096 to 16,384. When the number of Codex log files exceeds the old limit, usage no longer reparses part of them on every refresh. ⟦An office keeps one shared copy of identical forms and swaps in a filing cabinet four times the size, saving space while keeping old records from getting pushed out and recopied.⟧

The per-file cache limit rose from 4,096 to 16,384, so a Codex history with more files than the old limit no longer reparses part of itself on every refresh.

title.zh-TW: IDE 與 Cowork 用 Claude 也能更新額度
title.en: Claude quota updates in IDEs and Cowork too

body.zh-TW:
明明已經切進編輯器繼續跟 AI 對話，選單列上的數字卻好幾個小時一動也不動，也沒半點提醒。過去 usage 只從終端機底下的狀態列讀取 Claude 額度。但是 IDE（寫程式用的編輯器）外掛與 Cowork 不會畫出狀態列，選單列就只能停在最後一次終端機工作階段的數字。

現在只要狀態列超過 15 分鐘沒回報新額度，而 Claude Code 自己的快取有同帳號的較新數字，usage 就會改顯示快取數值並標出資料是多久前的。這份數字可能會落後 20 到 30 分鐘。

切換帳號後也不再顯示另一個帳號的額度。額度通知改按帳號分開記錄，從額度用完的帳號切到另一個帳號時，usage 不會把它當成額度重置。⟦過去只盯著玄關溫度計，沒更新就一直停在舊度數；現在它久沒動會改看氣象站紀錄並標出時間，不同房間的數值也分開記不再混在一起。⟧
body.en:
You switch into your editor and keep chatting with AI, yet the number in the menu bar sits unchanged for hours with no warning at all. Previously, usage read Claude quota only from the status line at the bottom of the terminal. However, IDE (code editor) extensions and Cowork never draw a status line, so the menu bar stayed stuck on the number from your last terminal session.

Now, whenever the status line has reported no new quota for more than 15 minutes and Claude Code's own cache has a newer number for the same account, usage shows the cached value instead and notes how old the data is. This figure can lag by 20 to 30 minutes.

Quota from another account is also no longer shown after you switch accounts. Quota notifications are now tracked per account, so switching from an exhausted account to another one no longer reads as a quota reset. ⟦Before, you only watched the entryway thermometer and stayed stuck on an old reading when it stopped updating; now, if it sits still too long, you check the weather station record with its timestamp instead, and readings from different rooms are logged separately so they never mix.⟧

entries: **New panel theme: Plush Pals.** Cream cards with a brown stitched rim, and eleven original plush animals that stroll along a row under the cards. One pal sits on each quota bar at its current percentage; it looks worried from 80% and falls asleep when the quota runs out (whichever of the 5-hour and weekly quotas is closer to the limit), and wakes up cheering when it resets. The pals speak up only when it matters, one speech bubble at a time: when a quota reaches 80%, runs out or resets; when a sleeping pal's quota is about 10 minutes from resetting (it stretches); when the current pace would empty a quota early (saying how long is left, and which other tool still has room); when Claude or Codex reports an outage and when it recovers; when today's usage passes yesterday's (the line cheers); on the day's first visit, with a greeting that fits (a weekly quota that just reset, a return after a few days, Monday or Friday, or the time of day); and after midnight. Now and then two pals in line chat or one dozes off. In December snow falls across the panel and a felt Christmas tree, a different one each day, stands at its end. Click a pal to see its name. Pick it from **⚙ Settings → Switch Panel**; there are now 18 themes. The panel always uses its light look, whatever the system appearance.

**Beginner Mode lets you mark terms one at a time and skips project names.** Press 4–6 to mark a single term understood; 9 still marks all three. Branch names, PR numbers, file names, paths and bare numbers no longer take the three hint slots, and every hint must appear in Claude's answer.

**Beginner Mode treats two names for one idea as one term.** Once you mark "分支（branch）" or "PR（Pull Request）" understood, "branch", "分支", "PR" and "pull request" stop appearing as new hints, and typing either name counts as knowing it.

**Beginner Mode loses fewer "understood" marks when two conversations save at once.** Each change now re-reads the term list right before saving. It also stops asking Haiku for terms while the term list is unreadable, and the 5-hour pause now follows that quota's own reading time and reset.

**Beginner Mode explanations are no longer cut off mid-sentence.** Haiku is asked for a complete short phrase, and the length limit doubles to 80 characters. An explanation saved half-finished is replaced the next time its term comes up.

**Beginner Mode hints only what the answer really uses.** A term learned under one name no longer comes back under its other name, whichever came first. `API` no longer counts as appearing just because the answer says `RAPID`. PR numbers like `PR #42`, Windows paths and branch names such as `fix/test` no longer take hint slots, and one malformed term after a line of preamble no longer drops the others. Each reply also reads the term list fewer times.

title.zh-TW: 面板新增「絨毛小夥伴」主題
title.en: New "Plush Pals" Panel Theme

body.zh-TW:
查看用量想少點枯燥，現在有動物陪你看額度。到 **⚙ 設定 → 切換面板** 選「絨毛小夥伴」，共 18 種主題，固定亮色不受系統深淺影響。米白卡片配咖啡縫邊，底下 11 個原創絨毛角色散步，點選看名字，偶爾聊天打盹。

每條額度進度條站一位角色，停在目前百分比。5 小時與週額度較近上限那條用到 80% 會緊張，用完睡著，重置時醒來歡呼。

小夥伴只在要緊時出泡泡，一次一個：額度到 80%、用完與重置，或睡著後重置前約 10 分鐘伸懶腰。現速將提前用完會報剩餘時間，並推薦有空位的工具。Claude 或 Codex 回報故障及恢復時也會出現泡泡。今日用量超昨天整排歡呼，過半夜也有泡泡。每天首次造訪時，依週額度剛重置、隔幾天回來、週一或週五，或當下時段換招呼。12 月飄雪，隊尾日換一棵毛氈聖誕樹。

⟦過去只盯數字，現在公仔見底打盹、補滿歡呼。⟧

On each day's first visit, the greeting adapts to a freshly reset weekly quota, returning after a few days, Monday or Friday, or the time of day. In December, snow falls, and a different felt Christmas tree stands at the end of the line each day.

⟦Picture staring only at numbers before, whereas now plushies doze off at empty and cheer when refilled.⟧

title.zh-TW: 新手模式選詞更準並可單獨標懂名詞
title.en: Beginner Mode Picks Better Terms and Marks Them One by One

body.zh-TW:
用新手模式學名詞，以前只懂一兩個詞卻得按 9 全標，還常被無關的檔名或路徑佔掉三個提示位置。現在按 4～6 就能單獨標懂對應的那一個名詞，按 9 照舊三個一起標。分支名稱、檔名、路徑、單獨數字與 PR（請求把修改併回主線）編號不再佔位，每個提示也都會真的出現在 Claude 的回答裡。

同一概念的兩種寫法現在也算同一個詞。標過「分支」或「branch」懂了，兩者就不再當新詞提示；標過「PR」或「Pull Request」懂了，「PR」和「pull request」也不會再跳出。上述詞彙只要自己打出任一種寫法，就算你會了。

⟦以前背詞像整串鑰匙一起收、還常夾進門牌號，現在能拆開單獨收好，同一把的中英文兩把也只要認得一支就算過關。⟧
body.en:
When learning terms in Beginner Mode, you previously had to press 9 to mark all three even if you only knew one or two, and unrelated file names or paths often took up the three hint slots. Now pressing 4–6 marks just the corresponding term understood, while 9 still marks all three. Branch names, file names, paths, bare numbers, and PR (pull request) numbers no longer take up slots, and every hint actually appears in Claude's reply.

Two names for the same concept now count as one term. Once you mark "分支" or "branch" understood, neither appears as a new hint; once you mark "PR" or "Pull Request" understood, "PR" and "pull request" stop popping up too. Typing either form of those terms yourself counts as knowing it.

⟦Think of studying terms before like putting away a whole keyring with house numbers mixed in; now you can unclip and store each key on its own, and recognizing either the Chinese or English copy of the same key counts.⟧

title.zh-TW: 新手模式紀錄保存與提示比對更可靠
title.en: Beginner Mode Saves Progress and Matches Hints More Reliably

body.zh-TW:
多視窗存檔打架與解答斷句這類新手模式的小狀況，現在都有解了。

兩個對話同時存檔時，每次改動都在存檔前一刻重讀名詞紀錄，較不會弄丟「懂了」。紀錄讀不到時不再先請 Haiku 挑詞，5 小時額度的暫停改看該額度自己的讀取與重置時間。

白話解釋改請 Haiku 寫出完整短句，長度上限加倍到 80 個字元，不再被切成半句。之前存成半句的解釋，下次那個詞再出現時會換成完整版。

用一種寫法學會的詞，不論先遇到哪種寫法，換另一種都不會再回來。回答只有 `RAPID` 字樣時不再算出現 `API`，`PR #42`、Windows 路徑與 `fix/test` 分支名也不再佔位。Haiku 在清單前多寫一句話時，缺欄位的單一詞彙不再連累其他詞消失，每則回答讀名詞紀錄的次數也變少。

現在多視窗並行時，標記較不易漏存、解釋看得到整句，提示也只留回答真正用到的詞。
body.en:
Small Beginner Mode hiccups like competing window saves and cut-off explanations are now fixed.

When two conversations save at once, each change re-reads the term list right before saving so "understood" marks are less likely to be lost. When the list is unreadable, it no longer asks Haiku for terms first, and the 5-hour quota pause now follows that quota's own reading and reset times.

Plain-language explanations now ask Haiku for a complete short sentence, and the length limit doubles to 80 characters so they are no longer cut in half. Any explanation saved half-finished is replaced with the full version the next time that term appears.

A term learned under one spelling never comes back under the other, whichever you saw first. Replies containing only `RAPID` no longer count as showing `API`, and `PR #42`, Windows paths, and `fix/test` branch names no longer take up slots. When Haiku adds a line of preamble before the list, a single term with a missing field no longer causes the other terms to disappear, and each reply reads the term list fewer times.

Now when multiple windows run in parallel, marks are less likely to drop, explanations show full sentences, and hints keep only the terms the reply actually uses.

items.original:
**Beginner Mode loses fewer "understood" marks when two conversations save at once.** Each change now re-reads the term list right before saving. It also stops asking Haiku for terms while the term list is unreadable, and the 5-hour pause now follows that quota's own reading time and reset.
**Beginner Mode explanations are no longer cut off mid-sentence.** Haiku is asked for a complete short phrase, and the length limit doubles to 80 characters. An explanation saved half-finished is replaced the next time its term comes up.
**Beginner Mode hints only what the answer really uses.** A term learned under one name no longer comes back under its other name, whichever came first. `API` no longer counts as appearing just because the answer says `RAPID`. PR numbers like `PR #42`, Windows paths and branch names such as `fix/test` no longer take hint slots, and one malformed term after a line of preamble no longer drops the others. Each reply also reads the term list fewer times.

entries: **Every panel shows that the project range button cycles.** The button reads `Today ⇄`, matching the Antigravity `Gemini ⇄` button, so it is clear that clicking it steps through Today, Yesterday, 7 Days, Month and All Time.

**The Windows 95 panel uses three text sizes instead of six.** Card titles, row labels, percentages and the daily total are 15 px; project rows, the rate line and every button are 13 px; reset times, costs and the credit line are 11 px. Before this, card titles were smaller than the rows below them, and the `Gemini ⇄` button was smaller than the other title-bar buttons.
**Project bars in the Windows 95 panel are easier to compare.** They were 3 px tall, and the beveled border left about 1 px of green. They are now 8 px tall, 9 px for the top project.

**The Newspaper panel looks like one design.** Project bars were thin rounded strips; they now use the same square, outlined track as the quota bars. The `Gemini ⇄` button is square like the settings button instead of pill-shaped, and the Antigravity icon sits on a gray square like the Claude Code icon.

**The Antigravity header in the Cloud Observation panel is easier to read.** The `Gemini ⇄` button used a pale purple that nearly disappeared on the white glass card; it now uses the same deep purple as the Antigravity icon. The icon's backing circle, which was translucent white, is now light purple, so it no longer blends into the card.

**The bottom card in the Cloud Observation, Aquarium and Prism Arcade panels has more room.** The rate line and the daily total sat 5 px from the divider between them; the gap is now 8 px on each side, matching the space above the buttons.

**The Prism Arcade project card has an icon instead of the letter `P`.** It now shows a folder with small bars, in the same badge as the Antigravity and Grok icons, so it no longer looks like a placeholder.

**The fallen leaves in the Maple Dusk panel's bottom corners look like they landed.** Each corner had three leaves crowded into about 50 px, some turned sideways or upside down and lying across the card border. Each corner now has one large and one small leaf, lying nearly flat with a soft shadow, below the bottom card.

**The Catppuccin panel shows project names in their real case.** Names were forced to uppercase, so `esun-daytrade` appeared as `ESUN-DAYTRADE`, and the daily total read `TOKENS` while project rows read `tokens`. Project names and the unit now keep their case; labels and buttons stay uppercase.

**The Catppuccin flavor switcher labels each swatch.** The four squares at the bottom had no text, and the three dark flavors looked almost the same. Each square now has its name below it (Latte, Frappé, Macchiato, Mocha), and the selected one is highlighted.
**The Heart Monitor panel's quota bars no longer touch the reset time.** The bar sat 2 px below the reset line, and its 80% tick rose into the text. The gap is now 6 px.

**The Origami panel no longer hides text under its dark folds.** The first-place rank badge was half light and half dark, so its white `1` disappeared. The folded corner at the bottom right of each card was dark where the last reset time sat. The badge is now two shades of deep blue, and the corner fold is smaller and dark only at its tip, so reset times, percentages and costs stay on light paper.

**The stars in the Black Hole panel twinkle.** Only 8 of 120 stars changed brightness, and only slightly, so the background looked still while the black hole turned. Now 40 stars fade in and out, each at its own pace, and the six largest flash a small four-point glint at their brightest.

**The butterflies in the Lepidoptera panel no longer hide the text they fly over.** They drift above the cards and reached 85% opacity mid-flight, so their outlines covered reset times, the Settings button and the status line. They now peak at about 45%, so the text stays readable while they still fly over the cards.

**Token counts in the panel show their unit again.** The `tokens` unit next to project and daily totals went missing when the panels moved to HTML in v0.5.0, so numbers like `567,641` had no label. Every panel now shows the full count followed by a smaller, quieter `tokens`, for example `567,641 tokens`. Counts stay exact and are never abbreviated. In the narrowest panels the project name is slightly smaller, so a 13-character name still fits beside a nine-digit count.

**The settings button stays at the right edge of the card.** Before this fix, hiding Claude Code moved the button to the next card but left it right after the card title, or right after the Gemini button on the Antigravity card. It now sits at the right edge, as it does on the Claude Code card.

**Pick Up Where You Left Off now hands over how the last session ended.** Before this fix, the note a new conversation received listed only commits Claude made, so merges, tags and pushes you ran yourself with `!` were missing, and Claude was always told to propose a next step even when the last round was finished. The note now adds Claude Code's own end-of-session recap, used only when nothing happened after it, or else the opening sentences of Claude's last reply. It lists merged PRs, created tags and pushes that succeeded, newest first, and tells Claude to say a finished round is finished instead of inventing a next step. Claude Code's compaction text is no longer shown as your latest request, messages you queued while Claude was busy are now included, a request you resent with more detail is listed once, and after `/clear` the note picks the conversation this window just cleared. The uncommitted-changes line now says it describes the current working directory, because it is checked when the new conversation starts.

title.zh-TW: 「接著上次做」會完整交接上回結尾
title.en: "Pick Up Where You Left Off" Hands Over the Full Session Ending

body.zh-TW:
換開新對話接手進度，以前交接筆記只列 Claude 做的 commit（版本存檔紀錄），你用 `!` 跑的合併、tag 與推送全漏掉。就算上個工作階段做完了，它仍叫 Claude 硬給下一步。

現在會帶上 Claude Code 的整場摘要，摘要後無新動作才用，否則改附它最後一則回覆的開頭幾句。它也會由新到舊列出成功的合併 PR（合併請求）、建立的 tag 和推送，並請 Claude 做完就直說做完了，別自己編下一步。

對話壓縮的系統文字不再被當成最新請求，Claude 忙時排隊送出的訊息也會收進來。補充說明後重送的請求只列一次，按 `/clear` 後優先接這個視窗剛清掉的那場。「沒提交的改動」改為說明目前工作目錄狀態，因為它在新對話開始時才檢查。⟦像交接班以前只抄自己經手的事，現在連對方動過的進度與結尾都寫進交接本，做完就直接結案。⟧
body.en:
When you opened a new conversation to continue your work, the handoff note used to list only the commits (saved version records) Claude made, missing every merge, tag, and push you ran with `!`. Even when the last session was already finished, it still told Claude to propose a next step.

Now it includes Claude Code's end-of-session recap when nothing happened after it, or the opening sentences of Claude's last reply otherwise. It also lists successful merged PRs (pull requests), created tags, and pushes from newest to oldest, and tells Claude to say a finished round is finished instead of inventing a next step.

Compaction system text is no longer treated as your latest request, and messages queued while Claude was busy are now included. A request resent with extra detail is listed only once, and after `/clear` it prioritizes the session this window just cleared. The "uncommitted changes" line now says it describes the current working directory, because it is checked when the new conversation starts. ⟦Just as a shift handoff used to record only what one person touched, the logbook now captures the other person's progress and how things wrapped up, closing out cleanly when the job is done.⟧

items.original: **Pick Up Where You Left Off now hands over how the last session ended.** Before this fix, the note a new conversation received listed only commits Claude made, so merges, tags and pushes you ran yourself with `!` were missing, and Claude was always told to propose a next step even when the last round was finished. The note now adds Claude Code's own end-of-session recap, used only when nothing happened after it, or else the opening sentences of Claude's last reply. It lists merged PRs, created tags and pushes that succeeded, newest first, and tells Claude to say a finished round is finished instead of inventing a next step. Claude Code's compaction text is no longer shown as your latest request, messages you queued while Claude was busy are now included, a request you resent with more detail is listed once, and after `/clear` the note picks the conversation this window just cleared. The uncommitted-changes line now says it describes the current working directory, because it is checked when the new conversation starts.

entries: **New panel theme: Maple Dusk.** Maple leaves drift down over a gold-to-violet sunset, behind and in front of violet glass cards that let the sky show through, with small piles of fallen leaves in the bottom corners. Pick it from **⚙ Settings → Switch Panel**; there are now 17 themes. The leaves stop moving when macOS Reduce Motion is on.

**The Muse quota card disappears once the subscription ends.** Before this fix, usage kept showing the last saved Muse quota after a subscription lapsed. Once its reset times passed, the card, the Claude Code quota line and the notifications treated that quota as unused. usage rechecked only after a new Muse conversation, so it never noticed. It now reruns the model-free `muse usage --json` at most every 5 minutes, which also brings the card up to date within about 5 minutes of using Muse instead of 30. When Muse reports that the account has no subscription allowance, usage deletes the saved quota without falling back to a `muse exec` model call, and the card disappears. It comes back once Muse reports quota again.

**A Codex window past its reset time reads 0% and Reset.** Before this fix, both its usage and its reset time showed `--`, which looked like missing data. It now matches Claude Code and Antigravity until Codex reports a new reading.

**An Antigravity day that was counted too high can now be lowered in the year ledger.** Before this fix, when a fresh recount matched the daily snapshot, usage kept the snapshot's missing record of which counting version produced each day. A day saved before the token-counting fix therefore stayed too high after upgrading. Only days replayed from the snapshot now keep the stored versions.

**The year report no longer shows two totals for the same day.** The report read or built its cached year before saving the new snapshot, so the detail showed the corrected total while the heatmap showed the old one, and that old year stayed cached for 6 hours. The snapshot is now saved first, and a verified recount of an outdated ledger day skips the cache.

**The year report includes this run's activity even when the ledger is busy.** If another process held the ledger lock for too long, the report fell back to the ledger on disk without the days counted in this run, then cached that incomplete result. usage now adds those days in memory and does not cache the incomplete report.
**usage no longer stops with an error when it cannot create the ledger's lock folder.** It now handles this the same way as a lock file it cannot open.

**A Muse 5-hour limit shows up as a current reading.** When Muse refused a request because the 5-hour quota was used up, usage kept the previous reading's check time. The card looked stale, the "used up" notification was skipped, and usage checked again sooner than intended. The refusal now carries its own check time.

**A newer Codex Spark reading no longer replaces the general Codex reading.** When the Codex database held a newer reading for the dedicated Spark quota, it replaced the general reading from the session logs, and a general-quota rejection looked expired. Readings for different quotas are no longer merged.

**Repairing Token Saver no longer replaces a newer hook with an older one.** When a prompt file or settings entry was missing, usage overwrote the installed Token Saver hooks with the copies bundled in the app, even if the installed ones were newer. usage now replaces a script only when it is missing or older, and restores just the missing parts, the same way it repairs the resume hook.

**Quota-aware mode says when Claude Code's own quota was last read.** The "Claude Code's own quota" line left out the "(last updated ...; it may have reset since)" note that the same windows carry elsewhere, so an old reading could look current. The quota-aware hook updates to 1.20.

**CSV exports show "—" for a project whose cost is unknown.** They used to write 0.00, which read as free. Both the app's export and the export inside a saved report now write "—", the same as model rows.

**An exported report reopens with the same date shortcut.** A report exported from a shortcut such as All reopened as a manual date range, without the shortcut and its history note. A report exported with hidden project names reopened with empty date fields. The export now stores the shortcut and restores it.
**Reports show Gemini 4 Neon by its short name.** The model table listed Antigravity's new Gemini 4 Neon models by their full IDs; they now read "Neon 4", like the other models.

With the timing and status of each quota separated clearly, checking remaining amounts in the panel no longer requires guessing.
